claim: In the grassland game, increasing the number of wolves reduces the ability of sheep to develop grass-collecting abilities because wolves catch and eat sheep, reducing the time sheep have to collect grass.
falsifier: In a multi-agent predator-prey simulation, vary the number of wolf agents while keeping other parameters fixed and measure the proportion of time sheep spend collecting grass or the amount of grass collected.

conditions: sheep agents attempt to collect grass
wolf agents catch and eat sheep
exclusions: limited to the grassland game with the reported agent counts and reward structures

title: Increase in the number–decrease in sheep's ability mechanism

claim: Global parameter resets during high-replay training are detrimental to reasoning performance, whereas targeted resets on specific components yield superior returns.
falsifier: Compare global reset and targeted reset on a different LLM and reasoning benchmark under high-replay conditions.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Scope of parameter reset for Reasoning performance
